newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bonds stable awaiting wage decision.
newsitem.headline: Australian bonds stable awaiting wage decision.

text.p: *Australian bond yields were little changed from Monday's close, recovering from the modestly higher levels seen in after hours trading, ahead of the "living wage" claim verdict.
*AIRC to hand down wage decision at 2.00 p.m. (0400 GMT).

According to an analysis by Deutsche Morgan Grenfall a A$12 per week outcome would add 0.5 percent to aggregate wage growth. Deutsche sees a A$10-12 award making 4.1 percent average weekly ordinary time earnings growth in 1997/98.
Such a result would not cause concern for the Reserve Bank, as it would keep wages growth within the Bank's 4.0 to 4.5 percent comfort zone.

Traders noted buying of long stock at the opening which otherwise prevented the market drifting lower, while the short end firmed in preparation for a moderate pay award and ahead of an expected benign quarterly CPI report on Wednesday.

The market's steady tone saw it reverse some of Monday's spread widening against the dollar bloc. U.S. Treasuries weakened on Monday in preparation of a US$17 billion two-year note auction later today and a A$12.5 billion of five-year note offering on Thursday.
